name: Green politics
summary: Green politics seeks an ecologically sustainable society built on ecological wisdom, social justice, grassroots democracy and nonviolence. It rejects growth for its own sake, opposes nuclear power, favours decentralised participatory democracy and generous public welfare, and distrusts corporate power and free trade. Views on markets range from eco-socialist to eco-capitalist, but the mainstream backs a regulated mixed economy.
scope: The global Green party family as it states itself in the Global Greens Charter (adopted 2001, political action section updated 2012 and later), the foundational document that Britannica describes as the shared statement of Green parties worldwide. National party platforms, such as the US Green Party's, are left out as an organisation's own choices, as are green conservatism, green liberalism, green anarchism and other variants, which are separate subjects. Statements the Charter does not settle are null.

sources.title: Global Greens Charter (Britannica)
sources.author: Bill Kte'pi, Britannica
sources.usedFor: Identifies the Charter as the shared statement of the world's green parties and lists its six principles.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Principles pursue general and complete disarmament while backing UN-mandated force.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Principles call for equal rights regardless of class.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Charter works for humane treatment and welfare of all animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The Charter calls for humane treatment of animals during breeding, transport and slaughter.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Principles commit to non-violence and a code of conduct restricting arms exports.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Charter works to regulate and reduce the arms trade and pursues general disarmament.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The Principles promote a multi-cultural society and equal respect for cultural and linguistic diversity.

ban-patents-on-life.rationale: The Charter refuses to accept the patenting and merchandising of life.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Charter backs civil-society organisations and multi-party systems with accountable representatives.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: The Principles commit to non-violence and the Charter supports the ICC for war crimes.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Preamble condemns centuries of colonisation and exploitation of the world's peoples.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Charter supports the separation of state and religion.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Preamble speaks of an ecological debt owed by rich nations to peoples impoverished by colonisation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Preamble condemns colonisation and exploitation.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Principles require that each adult has an equal vote in electoral systems based on proportional representation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Preamble holds that cooperation rather than competition is a prerequisite for guaranteeing human rights.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Charter calls consumption in industrialised countries excessive and wants a quality-of-life emphasis over consumption of goods.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Charter will challenge corporate domination of government and criticises corporate political funding.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Charter demands decriminalisation of consensual same-sex relations.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Principles honour and value cultural, linguistic, ethnic and religious diversity equally.

death-penalty.rationale: The Charter demands that the death penalty be abolished worldwide.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Charter says all should achieve economic security and the Principles call for meeting basic needs unconditionally.

decide-locally.rationale: The Principles place power and responsibility in local and regional communities, devolved to higher tiers only where essential.

democracy-best.rationale: Participatory democracy is one of the six principles, and the Charter condemns all dictatorships.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Charter condemns all dictatorships regardless of their political claims.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Principles promote relationships across lines of division and equal rights regardless of race.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Principles require equality between women and men in all spheres of social, economic, political and cultural life.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The Charter calls climate change the greatest challenge and demands a rapid transition to zero-carbon economies.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The Charter backs strengthening the UN, force only under a UN mandate, and a World Environment Organisation able to impose sanctions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Principles call for equal rights for all individuals regardless of gender, race, religion, class or origin.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Principles promote a multi-cultural society and equal rights regardless of ethnic or national origin.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Charter supports a moratorium on new fossil fuel exploration and development.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The Charter opposes any expansion of nuclear power and works to phase it out rapidly.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Charter demands abolition of the death penalty and upholds the right of defence.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The Charter works to implement a Tobin-Henderson or financial transactions tax.

force-without-un.rationale: The Charter allows force only under a UN mandate.

free-trade.rationale: The Charter says unfettered economic activity is put above the public good, opposes new WTO-rule trade agreements and wants environmental and labour agreements to override trade rules.

future-generations.rationale: The Preamble affirms responsibility to pass the Earth on undiminished to the next generation.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Charter demands legal recognition of transgender people.

gm-crops.rationale: The Charter calls for a worldwide ban on commercial growing of genetically modified crops.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The Principles promote respectful relationships across lines of division in a multi-cultural society.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Charter calls for equal opportunities for disabled people and fertility decisions free of coercion.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: The Charter treats the climate crisis as caused by emissions, noting Western countries' emissions to date.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The Charter calls for a complete ban on nuclear arms.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The Principles recognise indigenous peoples' rights to land and self-determination.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Charter holds collective rights of indigenous peoples to self-determination and land, and rights for future generations.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: The Charter says force may be justified to prevent genocide under a UN mandate, which is not defence against an attack.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Charter supports the International Criminal Court and wants torturers tried before it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The Charter works for universal access to communications and free, independent media.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Principles pursue general and complete disarmament including a ban on nuclear arms.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Charter upholds a just secular legal system and the separation of state and religion.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: The Principles require strict limits on corporate and private donations.

limit-growth.rationale: The Principles say continuing growth in global consumption and population must be halted and reversed and that material expansion has limited scope.

limit-population.rationale: The Principles say continuing growth in global population must be halted and reversed.

local-production.rationale: The Charter states a preference for local production where possible.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: The Charter works to establish an emissions reporting framework for transnational corporations.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Charter commits Green organisations to practise internally the democratic principles they seek in society.

military-superiority.rationale: The Principles say security should not rest mainly on military strength but on cooperation and development.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Charter supports the right of linguistic minorities to use their own language.

nation-first.rationale: The Charter commits its parties to act globally and to a global partnership, noting that the environment ignores borders.

national-church-status.rationale: The Charter supports separation of state and religion.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Principles call for equal rights regardless of national origin.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Principles respect the specific values of all forms of life, including non-human species.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Charter calls for aid, welfare, public ownership of water and public funding of elections, well beyond protection from violence.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Charter wants corporate welfare made transparent and subsidies to harmful activities phased out.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The Principles call for a complete and definitive ban on nuclear arms.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Principles require that all citizens may join the political party of their choice within a multi-party system.

open-government-data.rationale: The Charter upholds citizens' right to official information and calls for transparency in governance.

organic-representation.rationale: The Principles require multi-party systems with proportional representation and the right to join parties.

parents-choose-intersex-surgery.rationale: The Charter calls for protecting bodily autonomy including for intersex people.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Principles call for a democracy where citizens directly take part in the decisions that affect their lives.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Charter upholds the right to free and independent media.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: The Principles declare a commitment to non-violence as the basis of global security.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling a minority as a group is the collective expulsion the Charter calls to prohibit.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The Principles call for caution where knowledge is limited, and the Charter applies the precautionary principle to research.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Charter calls the eradication of poverty an imperative and directs aid to the poorest of the poor.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The Principles list promoting freedom and democracy as a way to remove the causes of war.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Principles say continuing growth in global population must be halted and reversed.

property-franchise.rationale: The Principles require that each adult has an equal vote.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Principles require that all electoral systems be based on proportional representation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Charter upholds citizens' right of access to official information.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: The Principles demand equal rights regardless of race and ethnic or national origin.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Principles require an equal vote for each adult.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Principles demand equal rights for all regardless of race.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The Principles place power in local and regional communities, devolved only where essential.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Charter wants corporations to obey the stricter of the environmental, labour and social laws of their home or host country, backed by emissions reporting rules for transnational firms.

religious-nation.rationale: The Principles promote multi-cultural society and equal respect for religious diversity, and the Charter separates state and religion.

religious-offensive-war.rationale: The Principles commit to non-violence and a culture of peace.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: The Charter supports indigenous peoples' land rights and self-determination.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Removing an ethnic group from the country is a collective expulsion, which the Charter calls to prohibit, and the Principles demand equal rights regardless of ethnic origin.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Charter says those who profit from common or natural resources should pay full market rent for use and damage.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Charter holds human rights universal and indivisible and rejects growth at any cost.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Charter calls for reform of the WTO, IMF and World Bank and for equity in global development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Charter works to increase government aid to developing countries.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Charter upholds a secular legal system and separation of state and religion.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Preamble expresses concern for the value of cultural heritage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Charter demands equal rights for same-sex relationships and supports local communities' calls for marriage equality.

say-in-proportion-to-effect.rationale: The Principles call for decisions made by those affected and the Charter gives affected citizens a right to take part.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Charter supports the separation of state and religion and a secular legal system.

separated-powers.rationale: The Charter supports separation of powers between the executive, legislative and judicial systems.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Principles require equality between women and men in all spheres of life.

single-official-language.rationale: The Charter supports linguistic minorities' right to use their own language.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Principles require elected representatives to be committed to transparency, truthfulness and accountability.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Charter works toward cancellation of developing countries' debt, especially the poorest.

state-harmful.rationale: The Charter calls for restructuring state institutions, strengthening local government and holds that national governments are responsible for upholding rights, so it keeps a state.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Charter separates state and religion and respects religious and spiritual diversity.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Charter supports the separation of state and religion.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Charter requires a multi-party system and electoral systems open to new and small parties.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Charter endorses taxes, including eco-taxes, a financial transactions tax and taxes on non-renewable energy.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: The Charter opposes any violation of physical integrity by torture.

total-state.rationale: The Charter concentrates power in local communities and upholds civil liberties and separation of powers.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Charter condemns all dictatorships regardless of their political claims.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The Charter wants the WTO bound by labour conventions and labour agreements to take precedence over trade rules.

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: The Charter says asylum-seekers must have access to fair processes and not be returned to risk of harm.

universal-morality.rationale: The Charter states that the human rights it endorses are universal and indivisible.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Charter commits to non-violence and a secular legal system.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Principles call for breaking down inequalities of wealth and power that inhibit participation.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Principles call for equal rights regardless of gender in economic life.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Principles call for equal rights regardless of gender and equality between women and men in political life.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Principles call for balancing the flow of resources from South to North and the Preamble names an ecological debt owed by rich nations.

notes: Rules 7 pass. The 2026-10-15 audit leaned on the Green Party of the United States platform and a Wikipedia overview and marked some answers as inferences; the US platform is one party's programme and is no longer used, and every answer now rests on the Global Greens Charter, the movement's own foundational text. Answers the Charter does not settle are null. Themes searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means, globalism. Searched for a full Charter PDF and further scholarship; the full text of SAGE and the Charter's PDF copy were not retrievable (the Charter is read from the Asia Pacific Greens Federation's HTML copy).
